FOREWORD This Indian Standard [ P : 116 I ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Test for Petroleum, Petroleum Products and Lubricants Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`.

1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard describes two procedures for measuring consistency of small samples of lubricating greases by penetration of l/4 scale cone or a l/2 scale cone. This test method includes procedures for the measurement of unworked and worked penetration. 1.2 Unworked penetration do not generally represent the consistency of greases in use, as effectively as do worked penetration. The latter are usually preferred for inspecting lubricating greases. hazardous 1.3 This standard may involve and equipments. This operations materials, standard does not purport to address all of the safety problems associated with its use. It is the responsibility of the user of this standard to establish appropriate safety and health practices and determine the applicability of regulatory limitations prior to use. 2 REFERENCES The Indian `Consistency penetrometer' standard. standard, IS 1448 [ P : 60 ] : 1971 of lubricating greases by cone is a necessary adjunct to this

3.3 Unworked Penetration

,

The penetration at 25�C of a sample of lubricating grease that has received only minimum disturbance in transfer to a l/4 scale or l/2 scale grease worker cup or dimensionally equivalent rigid container. 3.4 Worked Penetration The penetration of a sample of lubricating grease that has been brought to 25'C subjected to 60 double strokes in a l/4 scale or l/2 scale grease worker, and penetrated without delay. 4 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD

The penetration is determined at 25�C releasing the l/4 scale or l/2 scale cone assembly from the penetrometer and allowing the cone to drop freely into the grease for 5 seconds. 5 SIGNIFICANCE AND USE

5.1 This test method is applicable to greases of National Lubric.sting Grease Institute ( NLGI ) consistency numbers 0 to 4 and is intended for use only where the size of the sample limits the useoflS 1448[P:601: 1971.
NOTE - This method is not intended to replace full scale penetration as describ-d in IS 1448 [ P : 60 ]. Precision is better in full scale penetration method.

The procedures in this test method are widely used for specification purposes, however, no correlation with field performance has been established. 6 APPARATUS 6.1 Penetrometer

6.7 Spatula

Sufficient sample to overfill the cup of the grease worker shall be required. If the penetration by l/4 scale is greater than 47 or by l/2 scale greater than 97, at least three times the amount needed to fill the cup shall be required as only one result can be obtained in one grease cup.

HALF-SCALE C~NC by holding it securely in its raised position while cleaning. Do not permit grease or oil on the penetrometer shaft, as this can cause drag on the shaft assembly. Da not rotate the cone, as this may cause wear on the release mechanism. 7.4 Penetration Measurement

long enough to bring the temperature of the sample to 25"CkO 5�C. Transfer from the container a portion of sample, preferably in one lump to overfill the cup of the grease worker or metal container of equal inside dimensions. Make this transfer in such a manner that the grease will be worked as little as possible. Jar the container to drive out trapped air, and psck the grease with the spatula, with as li~ttle manipulation as possible, to obtain a cupful without air pockets. Scrap off the excess grease by moving the blade held inclined towards the direction of motion at an angle of 45", across the rim of the cup. DJ not perform any further levelling or smoothing of the surface throughout the determination of the unworked penetration. 7.3 Cleaning Cone and Shaft Clean the penetrometer test. Bending of the cone carefully before each cone shaft can be avoided

Place the cup on the penetrometer table making certain that it can not teeter. Set the mechanism to hold the cone in the zero position and adjust the apparatus carefully so that the tip of the cone just touches the surface at the centre of the test sample. Watching the shadow of the cone tip is an aid to accurate setting. Release the cone shaft rapidly, and allow it to drop for SOO&O'l seconds. The release mechanism should not drag on the shaft. Gently depress the indicator shaft until stopped by the cone shaft and read the penetration from the indicator. 4

7.4.1 If the sample has a penetration over 47 by l/4 scale or over 97 by l/2 scale, centre the cone carefully in the container; this sample can then be used for only one test. If the sample has a penetration of 47 or less by l/4 scale or 97 by l/2 scale, perform three tests in a single container spacing these tests on three radii 120 deg apart -and midway between the centre and side of the container so that the cone will neither strike the side of the container nor impinge on disturbed area made in a previous test. 7.5 Additional Testing

8.3 Working Transfer sufficient sample to the cup of the clean grease worker to fill it heaping full, mounded up about 6 mm at the centre, avoiding the inclusion of air by packing with the spatula. Jar the cup from time to time as it is being packed to remove any air inadvertantly entrapped. Assemble the worker and, with the vent cock open, depress the plunger to the bottom. Close the vent cock and place the assembled worker in the water or air bath maintained at 25�C to bring the temperature 5

Make a total of three tests on sample ( either in three containers or in one ), is described in 6.4 and report the average value, to the nearest 0'1 mm, as the unworked penetration of the sample.

IS 1448 [ P : 116 I : 1992 of the grease to 25 f 0'5�C. Then remove the worker from the bath and wipe off any water adhering to its surfaces. Subject the grease to 60 full double strokes of the plunger, completed in 1 min f5 seconds and return the plunger to its top position. Open the vent cock, remove the top and plunger, and return to the cup as much of the grease clinging to the plunger as may readily be removed. As the worked penetration of a lubricating grease may change significantly on standing, proceed in accordance with 8.3, 8,4 and 8.5 immediately. 8.3 Preparing Sample for Measurement Prepare the worked sample in the cup for testing so that a uniform and reproducible structure of grease would be obtained. Jar the cup sharply on the bench or floor and pack the grease down with a spatula to fill the holes left by plunger and to remove any air pockets. Scrap off the excess grease extending above the rim of the cup by moving the blade of the spatula, held inclinded towards the direction of motion at an angle of 45" across the rim of the cup retaining the portion removed.
NOTES 1 The jarring should be vigorous as required to remove the entrapped air without splashing the sample from the cup. In performing these operations, a minimum of manipulation should be used as an agitation of the grease may have the effect of increasing the working beyond the specified 60 strokes. 2 Particularly when testing soft greases, retain th,: grease removed from the cup in a scrapping to provide a full cup for subsequent tests. Keep the outside of the rim of the cup clean so that the grease forced by the penetrometer cone to overtlow the cup may be returned to the cup prior to preparing the sample for the next test.
